chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her head-covering (micnah) and places it on her head, then he separates from her.

key_terms.الْأَخْرَسِ: The mute (person), specifically referring to the female in this context
key_terms.مِقْنَعَتَهَا: Her head-covering or veil, used here as a symbolic instrument for the divorce act
key_terms.يَعْتَزِلَهَا: He separates from her, indicating the completion of the divorce act

ai.seo_question: How is a divorce legally executed for a mute woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a specific legal mechanism for divorcing a mute woman, addressing the practical challenge of her inability to verbally acknowledge the pronouncement. By having the husband place her head-covering (*micnah*) on her head as a visible sign of status change before separating, the procedure ensures clarity and validity in the absence of speech. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on observable actions (*fi'l*) as valid substitutes for verbal declarations in marital contracts.
